Lemma 6.17
.

The map
\mathfrak{s}
defined above is an additive realization of
\mathbb{E}
.

Proof.

We first show that
\mathfrak{s}
is a realization.
Suppose we have
\delta=[X]\in\mathbb{E}(C,A)
,
\delta^{\prime}=[X^{\prime}]\in\mathbb{E}(C^{\prime},A^{\prime})
,
\overline{a}:A\rightarrow A^{\prime}
and
\overline{c}:C\rightarrow C^{\prime}
such that
\overline{a}_{*}[X]=\overline{c}^{*}[X^{\prime}]=[X^{\prime\prime}]\in\mathbb{E}(C,A^{\prime})
. Put
\mathfrak{s}(\delta)=[A\xrightarrow{\overline{f}}B\xrightarrow{\overline{\jmath}}C]
and
\mathfrak{s}(\delta^{\prime})=[A^{\prime}\xrightarrow{\overline{f^{\prime}}}B^{\prime}\xrightarrow{\overline{\jmath^{\prime}}}C^{\prime}]
.

We have a composition of morphism of conflations
X\rightarrow X^{\prime\prime}\rightarrow X^{\prime}
which restricts to
\overline{a}:A\rightarrow A^{\prime}
and
\overline{c}:C\rightarrow C^{\prime}
.
This morphism then gives a morphism
\overline{b}:B\rightarrow B^{\prime}
which makes the following diagram in
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
commutative

We now show that
\mathfrak{s}
is additive.
By definition, for
0\in\mathbb{E}(C,A)
, we have

\mathfrak{s}(0)=[A\xrightarrow{\begin{bmatrix}0\\
1\end{bmatrix}}A\oplus C\xrightarrow{[0{,}1]}C].

By Lemma
5.24
, we have
\mathfrak{s}(\delta\oplus\delta^{\prime})=\mathfrak{s}(\delta)\oplus\mathfrak{s}(\delta^{\prime})
.
∎

Remark 6.18
.

By Remark
5.4
, the exact dg structures on
\mathcal{A}
are the same as
the exact dg structures on
\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{A}
.
Note that we have
H^{0}(\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{A})=H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
.
By definition, the triple
(H^{0}(\mathcal{A}),\mathbb{E},\mathfrak{s})
remains unchanged when we replace
\mathcal{A}
by
\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{A}
.

By the above remark, the following theorem is a direct consequence of the fully exact embedding of
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
into
\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})
given by Theorem
6.1
. One can also prove it as follows: By Theorem
5.26
,
the dg nerve
N_{dg}(\mathcal{A})
carries a canonical exact structure in the sense of Barwick; this induces an
extriangulated structure on its homotopy category
h(N_{dg}(\mathcal{A}))
as shown by Nakaoka–Palu
[
110
, Theorem 1.1]
and we know that
the homotopy category
h(N_{dg}(\mathcal{A}))
is isomorphic to
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
.
Below, we give a direct proof of the theorem.

(H^{0}(\mathcal{A}),\mathbb{E},\mathfrak{s})

\lxSVG@closescope {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}\hss}\lxSVG@discardpath\lxSVG@closescope \hss}}\lxSVG@closescope\endpgfpicture}}.

So there exists an isomorphism
Y_{1}\rightarrow Y_{2}
in
\mathcal{D}(\mathrm{Sq})
which is compatible with the isomorphisms
R(Y_{i})\rightarrow S
where
R:\mathcal{D}(\mathrm{Sq})\rightarrow\mathcal{D}(\mathrm{Sp})
is the restriction functor.
So
[X^{\prime\prime\prime}]
can be realized by
D\xrightarrow{\overline{d}}E\xrightarrow{\overline{e}}F
such that
\overline{\jmath^{\prime}}=\overline{e}\overline{h}
. This shows (ET4). Axiom
(
ET4
op
) can be shown dually.
∎

Proposition-Definition 6.20
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be an extriangulated category. The following statements are equivalent:

1)

\mathcal{C}
is equivalent, as an extriangulated category, to a full extension-closed subcategory of an algebraic triangulated category.

2)

\mathcal{C}
is equivalent, as an extriangulated category, to
\mathcal{B}/(\mathcal{P}_{0})
for a Quillen exact category
\mathcal{B}
and a class
\mathcal{P}_{0}
of projective-injective objects.

3)

\mathcal{C}
is equivalent, as an extriangulated category, to
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
for an exact dg category
\mathcal{A}
.

If one of the above equivalent conditions holds, then
\mathcal{C}
is called an algebraic extriangulated category.

Proof.

Let us prove that 1) implies 2). Suppose the extriangulated category
(\mathcal{C},\mathbb{E},\mathfrak{s})
is equivalent to a full extension-closed subcategory of
\underline{\mathcal{E}}
where
\mathcal{E}
is a Quillen exact category.
Let
F:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow\underline{\mathcal{E}}
be the fully exact functor which is an equivalence onto its essential image.
Let
\pi:\mathcal{E}\rightarrow\underline{\mathcal{E}}
be the canonical quotient functor.
We form the following diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{B}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{E}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{C}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{\mathcal{E}}\mathrlap{\;.}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F}

Let
\mathcal{B}
be the full subcategory of
\mathcal{E}
consisting of objects
X
such that
\pi(X)
belongs to the essential image of
F
.
The category
\mathcal{B}
is extension-closed in
\mathcal{E}
since the essential image of
F
is closed under extension and
\pi
is a fully exact functor.
Note also that
\mathcal{B}
contains all projective-injective objects in
\mathcal{E}
.
So
\mathcal{B}
is canonically exact and the full subcategory

\mathcal{P}_{0}=\{P\in\mathcal{B}|\text{$P$ is projective-injective in $\mathcal{E}$}\}

consists of projective-injective objects of
\mathcal{B}
(but perhaps not all).
By
[
111
, Proposition 3.30]
,
\mathcal{B}/[\mathcal{P}_{0}]
has the structure of an extriangulated category, induced from that of
\mathcal{B}
.
The functor
F
induces a canonical equivalence of categories

G:\mathcal{C}\xrightarrow{{}_{\sim}}\mathcal{B}/[\mathcal{P}_{0}],\;\;A\mapsto F(A)

which, by definition, is a fully exact functor.

Let us prove that conversely, condition 2) implies 1). Suppose
\mathcal{C}
is equivalent to
\mathcal{B}/[\mathcal{P}_{0}]
as extriangulated categories.
Then we have a fully exact fully faithful functor

\mathcal{C}\xrightarrow{{}_{\sim}}\mathcal{B}/[\mathcal{P}_{0}]\hookrightarrow\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{B})/\mathrm{thick}(\mathcal{P}_{0}).

The triangle quotient
\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{B})/\mathrm{thick}(\mathcal{P}_{0})
is an algebraic triangulated category and
\mathcal{C}
identifies with an extension-closed subcategory of
\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{B})/\mathrm{thick}(\mathcal{P}_{0})
.

Let us show that 1) implies 3). Suppose
\mathcal{C}
is equivalent to a full extension-closed subcategory of
H^{0}(\mathcal{A}^{\prime})
for a pretriangulated dg category
\mathcal{A}^{\prime}
.
Let
F:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow H^{0}(\mathcal{A}^{\prime})
be the fully exact functor which is an equivalence onto its essential image.
Let
\mathcal{A}
be the full dg subcategory of
\mathcal{A}^{\prime}
whose objects are those in the essential image of
F
.
Then
\mathcal{A}
is an extension-closed subcategory of
\mathcal{A}^{\prime}
, since
F
is a fully exact functor.
By Example
5.7
,
\mathcal{A}
inherits an exact dg structure from that of
\mathcal{A}^{\prime}
.
By the definition of the biadditive functor
\mathbb{E}
associated with an exact dg structure,
we see that the inclusion
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})\hookrightarrow H^{0}(\mathcal{A}^{\prime})
is a fully exact fully faithful functor.
Thus
\mathcal{C}
is equivalent to
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
as an extriangulated category where
\mathcal{A}
is an exact dg category.

Let us show that conversely, condition 3) implies 1).
Suppose
\mathcal{C}
is equivalent to
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
for an exact dg category
\mathcal{A}
.
By Remark
5.4
, we replace
\mathcal{A}
with
\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{A}
and assume that
\mathcal{A}
is a connective dg category.
Then by Theorem
6.1
, we have a fully exact fully embedding
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})\hookrightarrow\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})
where
\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})
is an algebraic triangulated category.
∎

Remark 6.21
.

Item 1) shows that the class of algebraic extriangulated categories is closed under forming extension-closed subcategories.
Item 2) shows that the class of algebraic extriangulated categories is closed under forming ideal quotients by projective-injective objects.

In fact, the class of extriangulated categories can also be described using a seemingly more
general version of item 2) in Proposition-Definition
6.20
, cf. Corollary
6.49
for another proof based
on a similar idea. This generalization is suggested by a result of
[
37
]
,
stating that if
\mathcal{C}
is an extriangulated category and
\mathcal{I}
is an ideal generated by a family of morphisms

f:I\rightarrow P
from injectives to projectives, then
\mathcal{C}/\mathcal{I}
is naturally extriangulated.
In the context of algebraic extriangulated categories, we have the following result.

Proposition 6.22
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be an algebraic extriangulated category.
Let
\{f:I\rightarrow P\}
be a family of morphisms from injectives to projectives in
\mathcal{C}
.
Denote by
[I\rightarrow P]
the ideal generated by this family of morphisms.
Then
\mathcal{C}/[I\rightarrow P]
is still an algebraic extriangulated category.

Proof.

By item 2) of the preceding Proposition-Definition, we may assume
that
\mathcal{C}
is a Quillen exact category.
In
[
27
, Proposition 1.7]
, it is shown that given a full subcategory
\mathcal{N}\subset\mathcal{E}
of a Quillen exact category
\mathcal{E}
, the class of conflations which make the objects in
\mathcal{N}
projective-injective
is a Quillen exact structure on
\mathcal{E}
.
We endow
\mathrm{Mor}(\mathcal{C})
with the componentwise exact structure and view
\{f:I\rightarrow P\}
as a
full subcategory of
\mathrm{Mor}(\mathcal{C})
.
Let
\mathcal{F}
be the exact category whose underlying category is
\mathrm{Mor}(\mathcal{C})
and whose exact structure is
obtained from
\mathrm{Mor}(\mathcal{C})
by making the objects
f:I\rightarrow P
projective-injective.
Then
\mathcal{F}
is an exact category.
We have the inclusion functor

\theta:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow\mathcal{F}

sending an object
X
to
(\mathrm{id}:X\rightarrow X)
. Clearly, it induces a functor

\varphi:\mathcal{C}/[I\rightarrow P]\rightarrow\mathcal{F}/(I\rightarrow P).

We have the following observations

—

\theta
is an exact functor.
Indeed, a conflation in
\mathcal{C}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 0}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Y}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Z}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 0}

is sent, by
\theta
, to a conflation in
\mathrm{Mor}(\mathcal{C})

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces I}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 0}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Y}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Z}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 0}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces P}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 0}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Y}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Z}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 0}

For any morphism from
I\rightarrow P
to
\mathrm{id}:Z\rightarrow Z
, the morphism
P\rightarrow Z
factors through
Y
since
P
is projective in
\mathcal{C}
.
This shows that the morphism from
I\rightarrow P
to
\mathrm{id}:Z\rightarrow Z
factors through
\mathrm{id}:Y\rightarrow Y
.
Hence the objects
I\rightarrow P
are projective with respect to the conflations in the essential image of
\theta
.
Dually, one shows that they are injective.
Hence the functor
\theta
sends conflations to conflations in
\mathcal{F}
.

—

The induced functor
\varphi
is also fully faithful. This follows by definition.

—

The full embedding
\varphi:\mathcal{C}/[I\rightarrow P]\rightarrow\mathcal{F}/(I\rightarrow P)
is fully exact.
Let
\mathrm{id}_{X}:X\rightarrow X
and
\mathrm{id}_{Z}:Z\rightarrow Z
be two objects in the image of the functor
\varphi
.
Consider a conflation in
\mathcal{F}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 0}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Y}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Z}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 0}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 0}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Y^{\prime}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Z}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 0\mathrlap{.}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha}

The map
\alpha
is an isomorphism in
\mathcal{C}
.
Hence
\alpha:Y\rightarrow Y^{\prime}
is isomorphic to
\mathrm{id}:Y\rightarrow Y
and the above conflation is equivalent to a conflation in the essential image of
\theta
.

—

By definition, the category
\mathcal{F}/(I\rightarrow P)
is an algebraic extriangulated category.

Therefore, the functor
\varphi
is a fully exact fully faithful functor from
\mathcal{C}/[I\rightarrow P]
to an algebraic extriangulated category and hence
\mathcal{C}/[I\rightarrow P]
is also algebraic.
∎

6.23.
Higher extensions

Let
(\mathcal{C},\mathbb{E},\mathfrak{s})
be a small extriangulated category.
In their paper
[
52
]
, for
n\geq 1
, Gorsky–Nakaoka–Palu defined the higher
extension bimodule
\mathbb{E}^{n}(?,-)
on
\mathcal{C}
as the
n
th tensor power over
\mathcal{C}
of
\mathbb{E}
.
Recall that a right
\mathcal{C}
-module
F:\mathcal{C}^{op}\rightarrow\mathrm{Ab}
is
weakly effaceable
if for each
C\in\mathcal{C}
and each element
x\in F(C)
, there exists a deflation
p:B\rightarrow C
such that
F(p)(x)=0
, cf.
[
78
, A.2]
and also
[
77
, Definition 2.6]
.
Dually one has the notion of weakly effaceable left module.
A
\mathcal{C}
-
\mathcal{C}
-bimodule
G:\mathcal{C}^{op}\otimes\mathcal{C}\rightarrow\mathrm{Ab}
is
weakly effaceable
, if for each

C\in\mathcal{C}
, the left module
G(C,-)
and the right module
G(?,C)
are both weakly effaceable.
By
[
111
, Corollary 3.5]
, for each
A\in\mathcal{C}
, the right
\mathcal{C}
-module

\mathbb{E}(?,A):\mathcal{C}^{op}\rightarrow\mathrm{Ab}
is weakly effaceable. It follows that the tensor powers

\mathbb{E}^{n}(?,-)
are weakly effaceable.

In the rest of this section, we will omit the symbol
∧
in the representable dg module
A^{\wedge}
for
A\in\mathcal{A}
.
Recall the extriangulated category
(H^{0}(\mathcal{A}),\mathbb{E},\mathfrak{s})
associated with the exact dg category
\mathcal{A}
.
Clearly
(\mathrm{Ext}^{n}_{\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})}(?,-))_{n\geq 0}
together with the connecting morphisms given by triangles in
\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})
induced by
\mathbb{E}
-triangles in
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
, is a
\delta
-functor (cf. Definition
A.16
) for
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
.
It clearly satisfies the assumptions
A.2
and
A.3
.

Proposition 6.24
.

Let
F:\mathcal{A}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A})
be the universal embedding of
\mathcal{A}

into a pretriangulated category.
Then we have a canonical isomorphism of
\delta
-functors
\alpha:\mathbb{E}^{n}(?,-)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Ext}^{n}_{\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})}(?,-)
.

Proof.

Put
\mathcal{C}=H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
.
Let us show the
\mathcal{C}
-
\mathcal{C}
-bimodule
\mathrm{Ext}^{n}_{\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})}(?,-)
is effaceable for each
n\geq 1
.

By construction, we have
\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})=\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})/\mathcal{N}
.
Consider a morphism from
C
to
\Sigma^{n}(A)
in
\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})
given by the roof

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces C}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{n}(A)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces s}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces w}

where
s
and
w
are morphisms in
\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})
and
N=\mathrm{Cone}(s)
lies in
\mathcal{N}
.
We may assume

.
By Corollary
6.12
,
N
is an extension of its homology which are defective objects in
\mathcal{H}
.
For defective objects
\widetilde{N}
we know that
\mathrm{RHom}_{\mathcal{A}}(\widetilde{N},A^{\prime})
is concentrated in degree
2
for
A^{\prime}\in\mathcal{A}
.
So we may assume
N\in\mathcal{N}^{[-n+1,0]}
and write

where

is defective for each
i
.
Suppose for each
i
,

is the totalization of a conflation

of the form

We have a canonical map

.

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma A_{n-2}}

.

which induces the morphism

.

The map from

to

gives rise to a morphism

.

.

Let

.
The map
\Sigma^{n-2}N_{n-2}\rightarrow N_{\geq-n+2}
gives rise to a canonical map
N_{\geq-n+2}\rightarrow\Sigma^{n}A_{n-2}
.
It induces a canonical map
v:\mathrm{Cone}(u)\rightarrow\Sigma^{n}A_{n-2}
.
We have the following commuative diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{-1}N_{n-1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{-n}N}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{-n}N_{\geq-n+2}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces N_{n-1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{-1}N_{n-1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{-(n-1)}M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{-n}\mathrm{Cone}(u)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces N_{n-1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{-1}N_{n-1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma A_{n-1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma V_{n-1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces N_{n-1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces x}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces y}

where
y
is the composition
\Sigma^{-n}\mathrm{Cone}(u)\rightarrow A_{n-2}\rightarrow C_{n-1}\rightarrow\Sigma V_{n-1}
.
Since the spaces
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(\Sigma^{-n}N_{\geq-n+2},\Sigma A)
and
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(\Sigma^{-n+1}C,\Sigma A)
both vanish, the space

\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(\Sigma^{-n}\mathrm{Cone}(u),\Sigma A)

also vanishes and hence the composition
\Sigma^{-n+1}M\xrightarrow{x}\Sigma A_{n-1}\xrightarrow{\Sigma a}\Sigma A
equals to the morphism
\Sigma^{-n+1}(w)
.
We have the following diagram in
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{-n+1}M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{-n}\mathrm{Cone}(u)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma V_{n-1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{-n+1}C}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces A_{n-2}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces C_{n-1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma A_{n-1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma A}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{-n+1}(s)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces x}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{-n+1}(w)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{-n+1}(t)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{-n}(v)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces b}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma(a)}

which shows that the morphism
w/s
is equal to the composition of
\Sigma^{-1}(v)/t
and a morphism
\Sigma^{n-1}A_{n-2}\rightarrow\Sigma^{n}A
.
Hence the left
\mathcal{C}
-module
\mathrm{Ext}^{n}_{\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})}(C,-)
is effaceable for each
n\geq 1
and
C\in\mathcal{C}
.
Similarly one shows that the right
\mathcal{C}
-module
\mathrm{Ext}^{n}_{\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})}(?,A)
is effaceable for each
n\geq 1
and
A\in\mathcal{C}
.
The conclusion follows from Corollary
A.17
.
∎

Let
\mathcal{A}
be an exact dg category and
N_{dg}(\mathcal{A})
the exact
\infty
-category endowed with the
corresponding exact structure, cf. Theorem
5.26
.
Then the extriangulated structures on
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
given by
6.16
,
which we denote by
(H^{0}(\mathcal{A}),\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{A}},\mathfrak{s})
,
and given by
[
110
, Theorem 4.22]
,
which we denote by
(H^{0}(\mathcal{A}),\mathbb{E}_{N_{dg}(\mathcal{A})},\mathfrak{s}^{\prime})
, coincide with each other.
Indeed, it is straightforward to verify that the canonical map
\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{A}}(C,A)\rightarrow\mathbb{E}_{N_{dg}(\mathcal{A})}(C,A)
determines a natural isomorphism of biadditive bifunctors.

To each exact
\infty
-category
\mathcal{E}
, Klemenc
[
91
]
associates its
stable hull

\mathcal{D}^{b}_{\infty}(\mathcal{E})
(
=\mathcal{H}^{st}(\mathcal{E})
in Klemenc’s notation) together with a fully exact fully faithful functor
\eta_{\mathcal{E}}:\mathcal{E}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}^{b}_{\infty}(\mathcal{E})
whose essential image is closed under extensions.
Put
\mathcal{T}=h(\mathcal{D}^{b}_{\infty}(\mathcal{E}))
and
\mathcal{C}=h(\mathcal{E})
.
The category
\mathcal{C}
carries a canonical extriangulated structure, cf.
[
110
, Theorem 4.22]
.
Then by construction
\mathcal{T}
is the Verdier quotient of
\mathcal{S}\mathcal{W}(\mathcal{P}_{\Sigma,f}(\mathcal{E}))
by its full triangulated subcategory of acyclic objects.
By the same reasoning as in Proposition
6.24
, we see that
\mathrm{Ext}^{n}_{\mathcal{T}}(?,-)
is a weakly effaceable
\mathcal{C}
-
\mathcal{C}
-bimodule for
n\geq 1
and thus coincides with
\mathbb{E}^{n}
.
Let
\mathcal{E}
be the exact
\infty
-category
N_{dg}(\mathcal{A})
.
Let
F:\mathcal{A}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A})
be the universal exact morphism into a pretriangulated dg category in
\mathrm{Hqe}
.
Then the morphism
N_{dg}(F):N_{dg}(\mathcal{A})\rightarrow N_{dg}(\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A}))
induces a morphism
\varphi_{\mathcal{A}}:\mathcal{D}^{b}_{\infty}(N_{dg}(\mathcal{A}))\rightarrow N_{dg}(\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A}))
of stable
\infty
-categories.
By the above, this morphism is an equivalence of stable
\infty
-categories.

Theorem 6.25
.

There is a commutative diagram up to a canonical isomorphism

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\{\text{Exact dg categories}\}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\{\text{Exact $\infty$-categories}\}}

\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces N_{dg}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{D}^{b}_{\infty}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces N_{dg}}

Remark 6.26
.

In the preprint
[
35
]
, for an exact
\infty
-category
\mathcal{E}
, Børve–Trygsland defined an
\infty\mbox{-}
category
\mathcal{E}xt_{\mathcal{E}}^{n}(B,A)
for each pair of objects
(B,A)
in
\mathcal{E}
and
n\geq 0
whose
\pi_{0}
is naturally isomorphic to the
n\mbox{-}
th extension
\mathrm{Ext}^{n}_{h(\mathcal{E})}(B,A)
of the extriangulated category
h(\mathcal{E})
.

Example 6.27
.

Let
A
be a
k
-algebra and
n\geq 1
an integer.
Let
\mathcal{H}^{[-n,0]}(\mathrm{proj}\,A)
be the full subcategory of
\mathcal{T}=\mathcal{H}^{b}(\mathrm{proj}\,A)
consisting of complexes of projectives concentrated in degrees from
-n
to
0
.
Let
\mathcal{A}^{\prime}=\mathcal{C}^{[-n,0]}_{dg}(\mathrm{proj}\,A)
be the canonical dg enhancement of
\mathcal{H}^{[-n,0]}(\mathrm{proj}\,A)
.
We endow it with the exact dg structure inherited from
\mathcal{C}^{b}_{dg}(\mathrm{proj}\,A)
as an extension-closed subcategory.
Let
\mathcal{A}=\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{A}^{\prime}
with the induced exact dg structure.
We claim that
\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A})
is quasi-equivalent to
\mathcal{C}^{b}_{dg}(\mathrm{proj}\,A)
.
Indeed, since
\mathcal{C}^{b}_{dg}(\mathrm{proj}\,A)
is pretriangulated, the exact inclusion

\mathcal{C}^{[-n,0]}_{dg}(\mathrm{proj}\,A)\to\mathcal{C}^{b}_{dg}(\mathrm{proj}\,A)
extends to a canonical exact dg functor

\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A})\to\mathcal{C}^{b}_{dg}(\mathrm{proj}\,A)
. Its image contains
\mathrm{proj}\,A
so to show that it is an
equivalence, it suffices to show that it is fully faithful. For this, observe that
the category
\mathcal{H}^{[-n,0]}(\mathrm{proj}\,A)
has enough projective objects and the full
subcategory of projective objects is
\mathrm{proj}\,A
.
Then for each
P^{\cdot}\in\mathcal{H}^{[-n,0]}(\mathrm{proj}\,A)
we have a conflation

\Sigma^{-1}P^{\leq-1}\rightarrow P^{0}\rightarrow P^{\cdot}.

Let
Q
be an object in
\mathcal{A}^{\prime}
.
Then for
i\geq 1
we have

\mathbb{E}^{i}(P^{0},Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Ext}_{\mathcal{T}}^{i}(P^{0},Q)=0.

By induction we have

\mathbb{E}^{i}(\Sigma^{-1}P^{\leq-1},Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Ext}_{\mathcal{T}}^{i}(\Sigma^{-1}P^{\leq-1},Q).

Then by
[
52
]
Corollary 3.21,
\mathbb{E}^{i}(P^{\cdot},Q)
is the cokernel of the map

\mathbb{E}^{i-1}(P^{0},Q)\rightarrow\mathbb{E}^{i-1}(\Sigma^{-1}P^{\leq-1},Q).

Since the space
\mathrm{Ext}^{i}_{\mathcal{T}}(P^{0},Q)
vanishes, we have
\mathbb{E}^{i}(P^{\cdot},Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Ext}^{i}_{\mathcal{T}}(P^{\cdot},Q)
.

6.28.
Quotients with respect to projective-injective objects

Lemma 6.29
.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be a connective dg category and
\mathcal{C}^{\prime}\subseteq\mathcal{C}
a full dg subcategory.
Let
\mathcal{B}=\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{C})/\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{C}^{\prime})
.
Then for
A,B\in\mathcal{C}
, we have
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{B}}(A,\Sigma^{n}B)=0
for
n>0
and
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{B}}(A,B)=(H^{0}(\mathcal{C})/[\mathcal{C}^{\prime}])(A,B)
.

Proof.

Since
\mathcal{C}
is connective, by Proposition
3.9
we have a canonical co-t-structure
(\mathcal{T}^{\geq 0},\mathcal{T}^{\leq 0})
on
\mathcal{T}{\coloneqq}\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{C})
which restricts to a co-t-structure on
\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{C}^{\prime})
.

Suppose we have a morphism in
\mathcal{B}
as follows

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces A}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma^{n}B}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces s}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces b}

where
s
and
b
are morphisms in
\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{C})
and the cone of
s
lies in
\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{C}^{\prime})
.

Take a weight decomposition of
P=\mathrm{Cone}(s)
:
\sigma_{>-1}(P)\rightarrow P\rightarrow\sigma_{\leq-1}P\rightarrow\Sigma\sigma_{\geq-1}P
.
Since
A
lies in the coheart of the co-t-structure,
A\rightarrow P
factors through
\sigma_{>-1}(P)
.
Hence we may assume
\mathrm{Cone}(s)\in\mathcal{T}^{>-1}
.

Since for
n\geq 0
we have
\Sigma^{n}B\in\mathcal{T}^{-n}
, the map
\Sigma^{-1}\mathrm{Cone}(s)\rightarrow\Sigma^{n}B
vanishes and hence the map
b
factors through
A
.
So for
n>0
, we have
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{B}}(A,\Sigma^{n}B)=0
.

Now assume
n=0
.
If a map
f:A\rightarrow B
in
\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{C})
factors through an object in
\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{C}^{\prime})
, then it factors through an object in the coheart, i.e. a retract of an object
W\in\mathcal{C}^{\prime}
in
\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{C}^{\prime})
.
Therefore it factors through an object in
\mathcal{C}^{\prime}
.

So
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{B}}(A,B)=(H^{0}(\mathcal{C})/[\mathcal{C}^{\prime}])(A,B)
.
∎

Definition 6.30
.

An object
P
in
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
is said to be projective if for each conflation

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Y}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Z}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces h}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces j}

the morphism
\overline{\jmath}
induces a surjection
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(P,Y)\rightarrow\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(P,Z)
, or equivalently, if
P
is projective in the extriangulated category
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
.

Dually we define injective objects in
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
.

Example 6.31
.

Let
\mathcal{A}
be a connective dg category such that
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
is additive.
Suppose that
(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{S})
is an exact dg category with the associated extriangulated category
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
being triangulated.
We show that
\mathcal{A}
is quasi-equivalent to the truncation of a pretriangulated dg category.

Since each morphism can be completed to a triangle, each morphism
f:A\rightarrow B
in
Z^{0}(\mathcal{A})
admits a homotopy kernel and a homotopy cokernel which are both homotopy short exact sequences.
Moreover
\mathcal{S}
must be the class of all homotopy short exact sequences.
The canonical functor
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})\rightarrow\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})=H^{0}(\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A}))
is a fully faithful triangle functor and its essential image contains a family of generators for
\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})
.
Hence it is a triangle equivalence.
So the connective dg category
\mathcal{A}
is quasi-equivalent to
\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A})
.

Lemma 6.32
.

When
\mathcal{A}
is connective, an object
P
in
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
is projective if and only if
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(P,\mathcal{N})=0
where
\mathcal{N}
is the full triangulated subcategory of
\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})
generated by the total dg modules of conflations.

Proof.

Notice that the totalization
N
of a conflation

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Y}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Z}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces h}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces j}

lies in the heart of the canonical t-structure of
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})
and is the cokernel of the map

\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(-,Y)\rightarrow\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(-,Z).

Also for objects
A^{\prime}
in
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
, we have
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(A^{\prime},\Sigma^{i}N)=0
for
i\neq 0
.

So
P
is projective if and only if
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(P,N)=0
for each totalization
N
of a conflation.
∎

Let
F:\mathcal{A}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A})
be the universal exact morphism from a connective exact dg category
\mathcal{A}
into a pretriangulated dg category
\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A})
.
Recall that we put
\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})=H^{0}(\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A}))
.
Let
(\mathcal{T}^{>0},\mathcal{T}^{\leq 0})
be the canonical co-t-structure on
\mathcal{T}=\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})
introduced in Proposition
3.9
.

Since we have

\mathcal{T}^{\geq 0}=\bigcup_{i\geq 0}\mathcal{H}[-i]*\mathcal{H}[-i+1]*\cdots*\mathcal{H}

where
\mathcal{H}
is the coheart of the co-t-structure consisting of direct summands of
A
in
\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})
for
A\in\mathcal{A}
, it follows from Theorem
6.1
that
\tau_{\leq 0}\mathrm{RHom}_{\mathcal{A}}(A,M)
is quasi-isomorphic to
\tau_{\leq 0}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A})}(A,M)
for
A\in\mathcal{A}
and
M\in\mathcal{T}^{\geq 0}
.

If
P
is a projective object in the extriangulated category
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
, then by Lemma
6.32

P
lies in the left orthogonal of
\mathcal{N}
and we have

\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(P,X)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})}(FP,X)

for any
X\in\mathrm{pretr}(\mathcal{A})
.

Lemma 6.33
.

Let
\mathcal{P}
be a full dg subcategory of
\mathcal{A}
consisting of projective-injective objects in
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
.
Let
\mathcal{B}=\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})/\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{P})

We have

(6.33.1)

\displaystyle\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{T}}(M,\Sigma^{n}B)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})}(M,\Sigma^{n}B)

for
n\leq 0
.
So we have
b=F(b^{\prime})
for some morphism
b^{\prime}
in
\mathcal{T}
.

This shows that
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{B}}(A,\Sigma^{n}B)\rightarrow\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{B}^{\prime}}(A,\Sigma^{n}B)
is a surjection for
n\leq 0
.

Assume the morphism
b=F(b^{\prime}):M\rightarrow\Sigma^{n}B
in
\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})
factors through an object in
\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{P})
.
By the bijection
6.33.1
and since
\mathcal{P}
consists of projective-injective objects, the morphism
b^{\prime}
in
\mathcal{T}
also factors through an object in
\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{P})
.

So the canonical map
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{B}}(A,\Sigma^{n}B)\rightarrow\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{B}^{\prime}}(A,\Sigma^{n}B)
is a bijection for each
n\leq 0
.

2) For
n\geq 1
, since
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})}(\Sigma^{-1}P,\Sigma^{n}B)=0
for
P\in\mathcal{T}^{\geq 0}
,
b:M\rightarrow\Sigma^{n}B
factors through
A
.
So
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})}(A,\Sigma^{n}B)\rightarrow\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{B}^{\prime}}(A,\Sigma^{n}B)
is a surjection.

Let
f:A\rightarrow\Sigma^{n}B
be a morphism in
\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})
factors through an object
Q
in
\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{P})
.
We may assume
Q\in\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{P})^{\geq 0}
.
Then
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})}(Q,\Sigma^{n}B)=0
and hence the morphism
f
is zero.

So
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})}(A,\Sigma^{n}B)\rightarrow\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{B}^{\prime}}(A,\Sigma^{n}B)
is a bijection for
n\geq 1
.
∎

Let
\mathcal{P}
be a full dg subcategory of a connective exact dg category
\mathcal{A}
consisting of projective-injective objects.
Then we have the following diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces H^{0}(\mathcal{A})/[\mathcal{P}]}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})/\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{P})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})/\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{P})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G_{2}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces H}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F_{2}}

In summary we have

Proposition 6.34
.

Let
A,B\in\mathcal{A}
. The following statements hold:

1)

H
is fully faithful.

2)

For
n\geq 1
,
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})/\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{P})}(A,\Sigma^{n}B)=0
.

3)

For
n\leq 0
,
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})/\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{P})}(A,\Sigma^{n}B)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})/\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{P})}(A,\Sigma^{n}B)
.

4)

For
n\geq 1
,
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})}(A,\Sigma^{n}B)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})/\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{P})}(A,\Sigma^{n}B)
.
In particular, the essential image of
F_{2}\circ H
is closed under extension in
\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})/\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{P})
.

5)

For
n\leq 0
,
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(A,\Sigma^{n}B)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})}(A,\Sigma^{n}B)
.

For an extriangulated category
\mathcal{C}
with a subcategory
\mathcal{P}
consisting of (not necessarily all) projective-injective objects in
\mathcal{C}
, Nakaoka–Palu showed that the ideal quotient
\mathcal{C}/\mathcal{P}
has the structure of an extriangulated category, induced from that of
\mathcal{C}
, cf.
[
111
, Proposition 3.30]
. In the context of exact dg categories, we have the following theorem.

Theorem 6.35
.

Let
\mathcal{A}
be a connective exact dg category and
\mathcal{P}
a full dg subcategory of
\mathcal{A}
consisting of projective-injective objects in
\mathcal{A}
.
Let
\mathcal{S}_{dg}
be the canonical dg enhancement of
\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})/\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{P})
.
Then the dg quotient
\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{P}
carries a canonical exact dg structure induced from that of
\mathcal{A}
and its dg derived category is quasi-equivalent to
\mathcal{S}_{dg}
.

Proof.

By the items
(1)
and
(3)
of Proposition
6.34
, we have
H^{0}(\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{P})=H^{0}(\mathcal{A})/[\mathcal{P}]
and the canonical morphism
\varphi:\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{P}\rightarrow\mathcal{S}_{dg}
in
\mathrm{Hqe}
is quasi-fully faithful.
By the item (4), the quasi-essential image of
\varphi
is closed under extensions in
\mathcal{S}_{dg}
and therefore
\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{P}
carries a canonical exact dg structure.
Again by the item
(4)
and Proposition
6.24
, the bounded dg derived category of
\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{P}
is quasi-equivalent to
\mathcal{S}_{dg}
.
∎

Example 6.36

(
[
74
]
)
.

Let
k
be a field.
A dg
k
-algebra
A
is proper if
\sum_{i\in\mathbb{Z}}\dim_{k}{H^{i}(A)<\infty}
.
It is Gorenstein if the thick subcategory
\mathrm{per}(A)
of the derived category
\mathcal{D}(A)

generated by
A
coincides with the thick subcategory
\mathrm{thick}(DA)
generated by
DA
, where
D=\mathrm{Hom}_{k}(-,k)
is the
k\mbox{-dual}
.
Let
A
be a connective proper Gorenstein dg algebra.
A dg
A\mbox{-}
module is perfectly valued if its total cohomology is finite-dimensional and we denote by
\mathrm{pvd}(A)
the triangulated category of perfectly valued dg
A\mbox{-}
modules.
A dg
A\mbox{-}
module
M
in
\mathrm{pvd}(A)
is Cohen–Macaulay if
H^{i}(M)=0
and
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}(A)}(M,\Sigma^{i}A)=0
for
i>0
.
Let
\mathrm{CM}A
be the subcategory of
\mathrm{pvd}(A)
consisting of Cohen-Macaulay dg
A\mbox{-}
modules.
By
[
74
, Theorem 2.4]
, the category
\mathrm{CM}A
is an
\mathrm{Ext}\mbox{-}
finite Frobenius extriangulated category with
\mathrm{proj}\,(\mathrm{CM}A)=\mathrm{add}A
.
Let
\mathrm{pvd}_{dg}(A)
be the canonical dg enhancement of
\mathrm{pvd}(A)
and
\mathcal{A}^{\prime}\subseteq\mathrm{pvd}(A)
the full dg subcategory consisting of Cohen–Macaulay dg modules.
Put
\mathcal{A}=\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{A}^{\prime}
.
Since
\mathcal{A}^{\prime}
is extension-closed in
\mathrm{pvd}_{dg}(A)
, the dg category
\mathcal{A}
inherits a canonical exact structure whose corresponding extriangulated category is
\mathrm{CM}A
. Note that for projective objects
P\in\mathrm{add}(A)
, the Hom spaces
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}(A)}(P,\Sigma^{i}M)
vanishes for
i>0
and
M\in\mathrm{CM}A
.
By
[
74
, Lemma 3.9 (2)]
, the triangulated category
\mathrm{pvd}(A)
is generated by
\mathrm{CM}A
.
By the same reasoning in Example
6.27
, the bounded dg derived category of
\mathcal{A}
is quasi-equivalent to
\mathrm{pvd}_{dg}(A)
. By Proposition
6.34
, the stable category
\mathrm{CM}(A)/[\mathrm{proj}\,(\mathrm{CM}A)]
is equivalent to the singularity category
\mathrm{pvd}(A)/\mathrm{per}(A)
.

6.37.
Categories with enough projectives

Assume that the extriangulated category
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
has enough projectives and let
\mathcal{P}
be the full subcategory consisting of projective objects.
For a morphism
b:B\rightarrow B^{\prime}
in
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
, denote by
[b]
the corresponding morphism in
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})/[\mathcal{P}]
.
Put
\Omega^{0}{\coloneqq}\mathrm{id}:H^{0}(\mathcal{A})/[\mathcal{P}]\rightarrow H^{0}(\mathcal{A})/[\mathcal{P}]
.
For
n\geq 1
, we define syzygz functors
\Omega^{n}
as
n
-iterations of
\Omega:H^{0}(\mathcal{A})/[\mathcal{P}]\rightarrow H^{0}(\mathcal{A})/[\mathcal{P}]
which is defined as follows.

For each object
B\in H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
, we pick once and for all an
\mathbb{E}
-extension
\delta_{B}
which is realized by
\Omega B\rightarrow P^{-1}\rightarrow B
where
P^{-1}
is projective.
Since
P^{-1}
is projective, a morphism
b:B\rightarrow B^{\prime}
in
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
gives rise to a morphism
(r,b)
of
\mathbb{E}
-extensions

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Omega B}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces P^{-1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Omega B^{\prime}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces P^{\prime-1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\exists r}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces b}

Lemma 6.38

(
[
70
]
, Definition-Proposition 1.25)
.

B\mapsto\Omega B
and
[b]\mapsto[r]
define a functor
\Omega:H^{0}(\mathcal{A})/[\mathcal{P}]\rightarrow H^{0}(\mathcal{A})/[\mathcal{P}]
, which will be called the syzygy functor.

Proof.

By Corollary 3.12 of
[
111
]
, we have a long exact sequence

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cdots}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{Hom}_{H^{0}(\mathcal{A})}(P^{-1},\Omega B^{\prime})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{Hom}_{H^{0}(\mathcal{A})}(\Omega B,\Omega B^{\prime})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{E}(B,\Omega B^{\prime})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cdots}

The morphism
r:\Omega B\rightarrow\Omega B^{\prime}
satisfies
r_{*}\delta_{B}=b^{*}\delta_{B^{\prime}}\in\mathbb{E}(B,\Omega B^{\prime})
, so
[r]
is independent of the choice of
r
.
Also
b^{*}\delta_{B^{\prime}}=b^{\prime*}\delta_{B^{\prime}}
if
[b]=[b^{\prime}]
.

Therefore
B\mapsto\Omega B
and
[b]\mapsto[r]
define the syzygy functor
\Omega:H^{0}(\mathcal{A})/[\mathcal{P}]\rightarrow H^{0}(\mathcal{A})/[\mathcal{P}]
.
∎

For each object
B\in H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
, we have the following diagram in the dg category
\mathcal{A}

(6.38.1)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Omega B}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces P^{-1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Omega^{2}B}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces P^{-2}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Omega B}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Omega^{3}B}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces P^{-3}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Omega^{2}B}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cdots}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Omega^{3}B}

\scriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,1,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X^{-1}}
\scriptstyle{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces P^{\geq-1}_{B}}
\scriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,1,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X^{-2}}
\scriptstyle{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces P^{\geq-2}_{B}}
\scriptstyle{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces P^{\geq-3}_{B}}

where the rows are shifted totalized conflations and where we have omitted the homotopies in order to make it more readable.
We denote its totalization by
P_{B}
.
The totalization
P_{B}
carries an increasing filtration by the
P^{\geq-i}_{B}
,
i\in\mathbb{N}
.
Notice that
P_{B}^{\geq-i}
is homotopy equivalent to
X^{-i}
.

Claim 1: for each
Q\in\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{P})
, we have
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(Q,P_{B}^{\geq-n})=0
for
n>>0
.

Indeed for each
n\geq 1
, we have a triangle

(6.38.2)

\Sigma^{n}\Omega^{n}B\rightarrow X^{-n}\rightarrow N\rightarrow\Sigma^{n+1}\Omega^{n}B

in
\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})
where
N
is in the triangulated subcategory
\mathcal{N}
of
\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})
generated by totalizations of conflations.
Thus we have
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(Q,X)=0
.
Note that for
n>>0
, we have
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(Q,\Sigma^{n}Y)=0
for any
Y\in H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
.
So we have
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(Q,X^{-n})=0
for
n>>0
.
This proves Claim 1.

Claim 2: for each
Q\in\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{P})
, we have
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(Q,P_{B})=0
.

Indeed, we have a graded split short exact sequence in
\mathcal{C}(\mathcal{A})

0\rightarrow\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}P_{B}^{\geq-n}\rightarrow\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}P_{B}^{\geq-n}\rightarrow P_{B}\rightarrow 0

and hence we have a triangle in
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})
.

\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}P_{B}^{\geq-n}\rightarrow\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}P_{B}^{\geq-n}\rightarrow P_{B}\rightarrow\Sigma\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}P_{B}^{\geq-n}

By Claim 1 we have

\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(Q,P_{B})=\mathrm{colim}_{n\geq 0}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(Q,P_{B}^{\geq-n})=0.

This proves Claim 2.

Now let
A\in H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
and fix
m\geq 0
.
Then from the triangle

\Sigma^{n}P_{B}^{-n-1}\rightarrow P_{B}^{\geq-n}\rightarrow P_{B}^{\geq-n-1}\rightarrow\Sigma^{n+1}P_{B}^{-n-1}

in
\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})
, for
n\geq m+1
we have

\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(\Sigma^{m}A,P_{B}^{\geq-n})\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(\Sigma^{m}A,P_{B}^{\geq-n-1}).

It follows that we have

\displaystyle\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(\Sigma^{m}A,P_{B})

\displaystyle=\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(\Sigma^{m}A,P_{B}^{\geq-m-1})

\displaystyle=\mathrm{cok}(\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(A,P^{-m-1})\rightarrow\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(A,\Omega^{m}B))

\displaystyle=\mathrm{Hom}_{H^{0}(\mathcal{A})/[\mathcal{P}]}(A,\Omega^{m}B)

where we used the bijection

\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(\Sigma^{m}A,P^{\geq-m}_{B})\xrightarrow{{}_{\sim}}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(A,\Omega^{m}B)

given by the triangle
6.38.2
.

Proposition 6.39
.

Keep the assumptions as above.
Then the canonical map

\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(\Sigma^{m}A,P_{B})\rightarrow\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})/\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{P})}(A,\Sigma^{-m}B)

is a bijection for each pair of objects
A
,
B\in\mathcal{A}
and
m\in\mathbb{Z}
.
In particular, the canonical map

\mathrm{Hom}_{H^{0}(\mathcal{A})/[\mathcal{P}]}(A,\Omega^{m}B)\rightarrow\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})/\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{P})}(A,\Sigma^{-m}B)

is a bijection for each pair of objects
A,B\in H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
and
m\geq 0
.

Proof.

By the above Claim 1,
\{B\rightarrow P_{B}^{\geq-n},n\geq 1\}
is cofinal in the filtered category of morphisms with objects given by
B\xrightarrow{s}U
in
\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})
such that
\mathrm{Cone}(s)\in\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{P})
.
Thus we have

\displaystyle\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})/\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{P})}(A,\Sigma^{-m}B)

\displaystyle=\mathrm{colim}_{n\geq 0}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(A,\Sigma^{-m}P_{B}^{\geq-n})

\displaystyle=\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(A,\Sigma^{-m}P_{B}).

∎

Right triangulated categories were introduced in
[
87
]
(see also
[
78
,
10
]
) under the name “suspended categories”.
In loc. cit, they applied Heller’s stabilization procedure
\mathcal{S}
(
[
62
]
) to a right triangulated category and showed that this yields a triangulated category with a certain universal property.
They also showed that the stable category
\underline{\mathrm{mod}}{\mbox{}}A
of the category
\mathrm{mod}\mbox{}A
of finite dimensional right modules over a finite dimensional algebra
A
is left triangulated, and that its stabilization

\mathcal{S}(\underline{\mathrm{mod}}\mbox{}A)
is equivalent to the singularity category
\mathcal{D}_{sg}(A){\coloneqq}\mathcal{D}^{b}(A)/\mathcal{H}^{b}(\mathrm{proj}\,\mbox{}A)
.

Similarly,
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})/[\mathcal{P}]
is canonically a left triangulated category.
Here we indicate what are the triangles.

For a morphism
[b]:B\rightarrow B^{\prime}
in
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})/[\mathcal{P}]
, we have a morphism
(\mathrm{id}_{\Omega B^{\prime}},b):b^{*}\delta_{B^{\prime}}\rightarrow\delta_{B^{\prime}}
of
\mathbb{E}
-extensions

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Omega B^{\prime}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Omega B^{\prime}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces P^{\prime-1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces u}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces v}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces b}

where
b^{*}\delta_{B^{\prime}}
is realized by
\Omega B^{\prime}\xrightarrow{u}E\xrightarrow{v}B
.

Thus we get a sequence

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Omega B^{\prime}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{[}u{]}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{[}v{]}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{[}b{]}}

in
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})/[\mathcal{P}]
. We call such sequences standard triangles.

The distinguished triangles are defined to be those sequences which are isomorphic to standard triangles.

Proposition 6.40
.

The canonical functor
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})\rightarrow\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})/\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{P})
identifies
\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})/\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{P})
with the stablization of
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})/[\mathcal{P}]
.

Recall for each object
B\in H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
, we have a diagram
6.38.1
in the dg category
\mathcal{A}
whose totalization is
P_{B}
.

Let
Q_{B}
be the totalization of the diagram which is obtained from
6.38.1
by deleting the object
B
and such that
P^{-1}
is in degree zero.

For each
n\geq 1
, we take the totalization
Q^{\geq-n}
of the diagram obtained from
P^{\geq-n}_{B}
by deleting the object
B
and such that
P^{-1}
is in degree zero.

We have the following triangle

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Q_{B}^{\geq-i}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces P_{B}^{\geq-i}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Sigma Q_{B}^{\geq-i}}

in
\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})
.

The following lemma is a direct consequence of the above Claim 1.

Lemma 6.41
.

For
A,B\in H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
, we have

\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})/\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{P})}(A,\Sigma^{j}B)=\mathrm{colim}_{n\geq 0}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})}(A,\Sigma^{j}P_{B}^{\geq-n}).

Proof of Proposition
6.40
.

It is clear that the canonical functor
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})/[\mathcal{P}]\rightarrow\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})/\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{P})
is exact.
We only need to show that for each pair of objects
A,B\in H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
and
j\in\mathbb{Z}
, the following canonical map is a bijection

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{colim}_{i\geq 0,i-j\geq 0}\mathrm{colim}_{n\geq 0}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(\Sigma^{i}\Omega^{i}A,\Sigma^{j}P_{B}^{\geq-n})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{colim}_{n\geq 0}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})}(A,\Sigma^{j}P_{B}^{\geq-n})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha}

where an element in the left hand side which is represented by a morphism
f:\Sigma^{i}\Omega^{i}A\rightarrow\Sigma^{j}P^{\geq-n}_{B}
with
n\geq i-j+1
, is sent by the map
\alpha
to the morphism

A\rightarrow P_{A}^{\geq-i}\xrightarrow{{}_{\sim}}\Sigma^{i}\Omega^{i}A\rightarrow\Sigma^{j}P_{B}^{\geq-n}

in
\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})
.
On the left hand side, the map

\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(\Sigma^{i}\Omega^{i}A,\Sigma^{j}P_{B}^{\geq-n})\rightarrow\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(\Sigma^{i}\Omega^{i}A,\Sigma^{j}P_{B}^{\geq-{(n+1)}})

is induced by the canonical morphism
P_{B}^{\geq-n}\rightarrow P_{B}^{\geq-(n+1)}
.
The map

\mathrm{colim}_{n\geq 0}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(\Sigma^{i}\Omega^{i}A,\Sigma^{j}P_{B}^{\geq-n})\rightarrow\mathrm{colim}_{n\geq 0}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(\Sigma^{i+1}\Omega^{i+1}A,\Sigma^{j}P_{B}^{\geq-n})

sends an element represented by

with

, to the element represented by the morphism

\Sigma^{i+1}\Omega^{i+1}A\rightarrow\mathrm{Cone}(\Sigma^{i}P^{-i-1}_{A}\rightarrow\Sigma^{i}\Omega^{i}A)\rightarrow\Sigma^{j}P_{B}^{\geq-n}

where the latter morphism is induced by

.
Notice that for

we have

\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(\Sigma^{i}P^{-i-1},\Sigma^{j}P_{B}^{\geq-n})=0.

So the bottom row is also a bijection.

Claim: when
n=i-j+1
, the bottom row is an injection.
Indeed, let
r:A^{\prime}\rightarrow\Sigma^{j-i}P_{B}^{\geq-n}
be a morphism in
\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})
which factors through an object
N
in
\mathcal{N}
.
We may assume
N\in\mathcal{N}^{\leq 0}
. Since we have
n+j-i=1\leq 2
, the Hom space
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})}(N,\Sigma^{j-i}P_{B}^{\geq-n})
is zero.
Therefore
r
is zero in
\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})
and the bottom row is an injection.

We are ready to prove that
\alpha
is bijective.

1)

\alpha
is surjective: Let
f:A\rightarrow\Sigma^{j}P_{B}^{\geq-n}
be a morphism in
\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})
. We may assume
n\geq-j
and
n\geq 0
.
Let
i=n+j
. Then
f
factors through
P_{A}^{\geq-i}
in
\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})
.
In the category
\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})
, the object
P_{A}^{\geq-i}
is isomorphic to
\Sigma^{i}\Omega^{i}A
.
Apply the above bijection to
A^{\prime}=\Omega^{i}A
, and we get a morphism
\Omega^{i}A\rightarrow\Sigma^{j-i}P_{B}^{\geq-n}
in
\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})
.
This shows
\alpha
is surjective.

2)

\alpha
is injective: Let
g:\Omega^{i}A\rightarrow\Sigma^{j-i}P_{B}^{\geq-n}
be a morphism in
\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})
such that
\alpha
sends the equivalence class of
g
to zero.
So we may assume
n\geq i-j+1
and the map

A\rightarrow P_{A}^{\geq-i}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Sigma^{i}\Omega^{i}A\rightarrow\Sigma^{j}P_{B}^{\geq-n}

in
\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})
induced by
g
is zero. So the map
P_{A}^{\geq-i}\rightarrow\Sigma^{j}P_{B}^{\geq-n}
factors through
\Sigma Q_{A}^{\geq-i}
.
Since we have
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})}(\Sigma Q_{A}^{\geq-i},\Sigma^{j}P_{B}^{\geq-n})=0
, the morphism
\Omega^{i}A\rightarrow\Sigma^{j-i}P_{B}^{\geq-n}
is zero in
\mathcal{D}^{b}(\mathcal{A})
.

Put
i^{\prime}=n+j-1
.
Then the map
g^{\prime}:\Omega^{i^{\prime}}A\rightarrow\Sigma^{j-i^{\prime}}P_{B}^{\geq-n}
in
\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{A})
obtained from
g
is zero by the above claim.
This shows
\alpha
is injective.

∎

6.42.
Reproduction of exact dg categories

We show that “functor dg categories” with exact target and connective source carry canonical exact structures. Namely

Theorem 6.43
.

Let
\mathcal{A}
be a small exact dg category.
If
\mathcal{B}
is a small connective dg category, then
\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
is canonically an exact dg category.

In this subsection, it is convenient to work with
\mathrm{rep}(\mathrm{Sq})
instead of
\mathcal{H}_{3t}(\mathcal{A})
.
Recall that by Lemma
3.46
, we have a fully faithful functor
\mathcal{H}_{3t}(\mathcal{A})\hookrightarrow\mathrm{rep}(\mathrm{Sq})
whose essential image consists of homotopy bicartesian squares
X

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Y}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces N}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Z}

where
N
is acyclic.
Then an exact dg structure on an additive dg category
\mathcal{A}
can be defined to be a class
\mathcal{S}\subset\mathrm{rep}(\mathrm{Sq})
of homotopy bicartesian squares
X
, where
N
is acyclic, which satisfies similar axioms as those of Definition
5.1
.
We will use this definition in the rest of the section.

Remark 6.44
.

Let
\mathcal{B}
be the dg
k
-category
k\mathcal{I}
for a small category
\mathcal{I}
and
\mathcal{A}
a Quillen exact category considered as an exact dg category.
Let us compare the exact dg structure on
\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
with the Quillen exact structure on
\mathrm{Fun}(\mathcal{I},\mathcal{A})
.

Note that for objects
X
and
Y
in
\mathrm{rep}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
, we have

\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}\otimes\mathcal{B}^{op})}(X,\Sigma^{i}Y)\xrightarrow{{}_{\sim}}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B}^{e})}(\mathcal{B},\mathrm{RHom}_{\mathcal{A}}(X,\Sigma^{i}Y))

and the space
\tau_{\leq 0}\mathrm{RHom}_{\mathcal{A}}(X,\Sigma^{i}Y)
is zero if
i<0
, since the dg category
\mathcal{A}
is concentrated in degree
0
.
Thus we have a quasi-equivalence of dg categories

\tau_{\leq 0}\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})\xrightarrow{{}_{\sim}}H^{0}(\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}))\xrightarrow{{}_{\sim}}\mathrm{rep}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}).

Thus the canonical exact dg structure on
\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
provided by Theorem
6.43
induces a Quillen exact structure on
\mathrm{rep}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
.

The heart of the canonical t-structure on
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}\otimes\mathcal{B}^{op})
is equivalent to
\mathrm{Mod}\,(\mathcal{A}\otimes\mathcal{B}^{op})
.
Since the objects
X
and
Y
both have cohomology concentrated in degree 0, they belong to the heart.
So they are given by functors
\mathcal{A}^{op}\otimes\mathcal{B}\rightarrow\mathrm{Mod}\,k
and furthermore given by functors
F,G:\mathcal{B}\rightarrow\mathcal{A}
because
X(-,B)
and
Y(-,B)
are quasi-representables for each
B\in\mathcal{B}
.
So we have an inclusion

\displaystyle\mathrm{Fun}(\mathcal{I},\mathcal{A})=\mathrm{Fun}_{k}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})

\displaystyle\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Fun}_{k}(\mathcal{B},\mathrm{Mod}\,\mathcal{A})\xrightarrow{{}_{\sim}}\mathrm{Fun}_{k}(\mathcal{A}^{op}\otimes\mathcal{B},\mathrm{Mod}\,k)

\displaystyle\xrightarrow{{}_{\sim}}\mathrm{Mod}\,(\mathcal{A}\otimes\mathcal{B}^{op})\hookrightarrow\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}\otimes\mathcal{B}^{op})

whose essential image is exactly
\mathrm{rep}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
.

If we identify the categories
\mathrm{Fun}(\mathcal{I},\mathcal{A})
and
\mathrm{rep}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
via the above functor, we see that the Quillen exact structure on
\mathrm{rep}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
is identified with the componentwise Quillen exact structure on
\mathrm{Fun}(\mathcal{I},\mathcal{A})
.

For a dg category
\mathcal{A}
, denote by
\overline{\mathcal{A}}
the full dg subcategory of
\mathcal{C}_{dg}(\mathcal{A})
consisting of cofibrant quasi-representable dg
\mathcal{A}
-modules.
The Yoneda dg functor
Y:\mathcal{A}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}_{dg}(\mathcal{A})
induces a quasi-equivalence from
\mathcal{A}
to
\overline{\mathcal{A}}
, which we still denote by
Y
.

We may assume
\mathcal{B}
is cofibrant as a dg
k
-category.
For each
B\in\mathcal{B}
, let
R_{B}:\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})\rightarrow\overline{\mathcal{A}}
be the dg functor given by
X\mapsto X(-,B)
.
We have a morphism in
\mathrm{Hqe}
given by the following roof of dg functors

It then induces an (isomorphism class of) functor

for each small category

Lemma 6.45
.

Let
X
be an object in
\mathrm{rep}(\mathrm{Sq},\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}))
.
If for each
B\in\mathcal{B}
,
F_{B}(X)\in\mathrm{rep}(\mathrm{Sq},\mathcal{A})
is a homotopy cocartesian (resp. cartesian) square, then
X
is also a homotopy cocartesian (resp. cartesian) square.

Proof.

We show the case when
F_{B}(X)
is homotopy cocartesian for each
B\in\mathcal{B}
. The other case can be shown similarly.

By Corollary
3.47
, we may suppose
X
is of the form

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X_{0}^{\wedge}}

where

Let
W\in\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
.
By assumption, for each pair of objects
B_{1},B_{2}
in
\mathcal{B}
, and
i\leq 0
, we have

\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{A}}(X_{2}(-,B_{1}),\Sigma^{i}W(-,B_{2}))\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{A}}(C(f)(-,B_{1}),\Sigma^{i}W(-,B_{2}))

and hence for
j\leq 0
we have

\tau_{\leq 0}\mathrm{RHom}_{\mathcal{A}}(X_{2},\Sigma^{j}W)\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau_{\leq 0}\mathrm{RHom}_{\mathcal{A}}(C(f),\Sigma^{j}W).

Thus we have

\displaystyle\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})}(X_{2}^{\wedge},\Sigma^{j}W^{\wedge})

\displaystyle\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{B}^{op}\otimes\mathcal{A}}(X_{2},\Sigma^{j}W)

\displaystyle\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{B}^{e}}(\mathcal{B},\mathrm{RHom}_{\mathcal{A}}(X_{2},\Sigma^{j}W))

\displaystyle\xleftarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{B}^{e}}(\mathcal{B},\tau_{\leq 0}\mathrm{RHom}_{\mathcal{A}}(X_{2},\Sigma^{j}W))

\displaystyle\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{B}^{e}}(\mathcal{B},\tau_{\leq 0}\mathrm{RHom}_{\mathcal{A}}(C(f),\Sigma^{j}W))

\displaystyle\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{B}^{e}}(\mathcal{B},\mathrm{RHom}_{\mathcal{A}}(C(f),\Sigma^{j}W))

\displaystyle\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{B}^{op}\otimes\mathcal{A}}(C(f),\Sigma^{j})

\displaystyle\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{rep}_{dg}}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})(C(f^{\wedge}),\Sigma^{j}W^{\wedge}).

This shows that
X
is homotopy cocartesian.
∎

Lemma 6.46
.

Let
S
be an object in
\mathrm{rep}(k\mathrm{Cosp},\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}))
(resp.
\mathrm{rep}(k\mathrm{Sp},\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}))
).
If for each
B\in\mathcal{B}
, the object
F_{B}(S)
in
\mathrm{rep}(k\mathrm{Cosp},\mathcal{A})
(resp.
\mathrm{rep}(k\mathrm{Sp},\mathcal{A})
) admits a homotopy pullback (resp. homotopy pushout).
Then
S
admits a homotopy pullback (resp. homotopy pushout).

Proof.

We show the case when
S\in\mathrm{rep}(k\mathrm{Cosp},\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}))
. The other case can be shown dually.

By Corollary
3.47
, we may assume
S
is of the form

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X_{1}^{\wedge}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces PX_{2}^{\wedge}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X_{2}^{\wedge}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces j^{\wedge}}

where
X_{i}\in\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
,
i=1,2
and
j
is a graded-split surjection.

Since
j
and
PX_{2}\rightarrow X_{2}
are graded-split surjections, by assumption, for each
B\in\mathcal{B}
,
F_{B}(S)
admits a homotopy pullback

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces H(B)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X_{1}(-,B)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces PX_{2}(-,B)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X_{2}(-,B)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces j_{(-,B)}}

where
H(B)\in H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
.

Let
V
be the kernel of the map
X_{1}\oplus PX_{2}\rightarrow X_{2}
in
\mathcal{C}(\mathcal{B}^{op}\otimes\mathcal{A})
.
Then for each
B\in\mathcal{B}
, we have a canonical map
s_{B}:H(B)\rightarrow V(-,B)
.
By definition
G(B){\coloneqq}\Sigma\mathrm{Cone}(s_{B})
lies in the heart of the canonical t-structure on
D(\mathcal{A})
, which is equivalent to
\mathrm{Mod}\,(H^{0}(\mathcal{A}))
.
Note that the map
\Sigma V(-,B)\rightarrow G(B)
is well-defined up to a unique isomorphism.

For each morphism
b:B\rightarrow B^{\prime}
in
H^{0}(\mathcal{B})
, we have a canonical morphism
H(b):H(B)\rightarrow H(B^{\prime})
in
H^{0}(\mathcal{B})
which makes the following diagram in
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})
commute

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces H(B)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces H(B^{\prime})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces V(-,B)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces V(-,B^{\prime}).}

and it induces a canonical morphism
G(b):G(B)\rightarrow G(B^{\prime})
in
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})
.

Therefore we have a canonical functor
G:H^{0}(\mathcal{B})\rightarrow\mathrm{Mod}\,(H^{0}(\mathcal{A}))
which sends
B
to
G(B)
and
b:B\rightarrow B^{\prime}
to
G(b):G(B)\rightarrow G(B^{\prime})
.

By adjunction,
G
corresponds to an object in
\mathrm{Mod}\,(H^{0}(\mathcal{B})^{op}\otimes H^{0}(\mathcal{A}))
, which is equivalent to the heart of the canonical t-structure on
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B}^{op}\otimes\mathcal{A})
.
We still denote by
G
the corresponding object in
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B}^{op}\otimes\mathcal{A})
. We may assume
G
is cofibrant.

Our next aim is to find a morphism from
\Sigma V
to
G
in
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B}^{op}\otimes\mathcal{A})
.
We have the canonical isomorphism

(41.1)

\displaystyle\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B}^{op)}\otimes\mathcal{A}}(\Sigma V,G)

\displaystyle\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B}^{e})}(\mathcal{B},\mathrm{RHom}_{\mathcal{A}}(\Sigma V,G)).

We have that
\mathrm{RHom}_{\mathcal{A}}(\Sigma V,G)
is concentrated in degrees 0 and 1.
So

(41.2)

\displaystyle\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B}^{e})}(\mathcal{B},\mathrm{RHom}_{\mathcal{A}}(\Sigma V,G))\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Hom}_{(H^{0}\mathcal{B})^{e}}(H^{0}(\mathcal{B}),H^{0}\mathrm{RHom}_{\mathcal{A}}(\Sigma V,G)).

For each pair of objects
B,B^{\prime}\in H^{0}(\mathcal{B})
, we have the map

\alpha_{B,B^{\prime}}:\mathrm{Hom}_{H^{0}(\mathcal{B})}(B,B^{\prime})\rightarrow\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})}(\Sigma V(-,B),G(-,B^{\prime}))

where
b:B\rightarrow B^{\prime}
is sent to
\Sigma V(-,B)\rightarrow G(-,B)\xrightarrow{G(-,b)}G(-,B^{\prime})
where the first map is the canonical map.
It is not hard to check

\alpha_{-,-}:\mathrm{Hom}_{H^{0}(\mathcal{B})}(-,-)\rightarrow\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{A}}(\Sigma V,G)

defines an
H^{0}(\mathcal{B})-H^{0}(\mathcal{B})
-bimodule morphism.
By
41.1
and
41.2
, this defines a morphism
u:\Sigma V\rightarrow G
in
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B}^{op}\otimes\mathcal{A})
. By definition,
u_{(-,B)}
is the canonical morphism
\Sigma V(-,B)\rightarrow G(-,B)
.

Let
X_{0}
be
\Sigma^{-1}\mathrm{Cone}(u)
.
Then
X_{0}(-,B)
is quasi-isomorphic to
H(B)
for each
B\in\mathcal{B}
and hence
X_{0}\in\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
.
Consider the composition morphism
X_{0}\rightarrow V\rightarrow X_{1}\oplus PX_{2}
.
The sequence
X_{0}\rightarrow X_{1}\oplus PX_{2}\rightarrow X_{2}
then corresponds to a square

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X_{0}^{\wedge}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X_{1}^{\wedge}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces PX_{2}^{\wedge}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X_{2}^{\wedge}}

which is homotopy cocartesian and hence a homotopy pushout of
S
.
∎

Proof of Theorem
6.43
.

Let
\mathcal{S}
be the class of homotopy bicartesian squares
X\in\mathrm{rep}(\mathrm{Sq},\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}))
such that
F_{B}(X)\in\mathrm{rep}(\mathrm{Sq},\mathcal{A})
is a conflation for each
B\in\mathcal{B}
. By Lemma
6.45
and Lemma
6.46
, one checks that
(\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}),\mathcal{S})
is an exact dg category.
∎

Remark 6.47
.

From the definition of the canonical exact dg structure on
\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
, it is clear that an exact morphism
F:\mathcal{A}\rightarrow\mathcal{A}^{\prime}
in
\mathrm{Hqe}
induces an exact morphism
F_{*}:\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})\rightarrow\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}^{\prime})
in
\mathrm{Hqe}
.

Let
\mathcal{A}
be an exact dg category.
Recall that there is a canonical extriangulated structure
(H^{0}(\mathcal{A}),\mathbb{E},\mathfrak{s})
on
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
.
Let
\{I\xrightarrow{\overline{f}}P\}
be family of morphisms in
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
from injectives to projectives.
Let
\mathcal{B}
be the dg category
k\mathrm{Mor}=k(0\rightarrow 1)
.
Recall that if a morphism
f:I\rightarrow P
in
Z^{0}(\mathcal{A})
is homotopic to
f^{\prime}
, then the objects
f:I\rightarrow P
and
f^{\prime}:I\rightarrow P
are isomorphic in
\mathrm{rep}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
.
Thus we may consider the family of objects
I\xrightarrow{{f}}P
in
\mathrm{rep}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
.
We may assume
\{I\rightarrow P\}
forms an additive subcategory of
\mathrm{rep}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
.
Let
\mathcal{J}
be the ideal in
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
consisting of morphisms which factor through morphisms in the family
\{I\rightarrow P\}
.

By Theorem
6.43
,
\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
is canonically an exact dg category. Consider the exact dg substructure of
\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
which makes the objects represented by
I\rightarrow P
projective-injective. We have an equivalence of categories
\mathrm{rep}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})\xrightarrow{\sim}H^{0}(\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}))
where
H^{0}(\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}))
is identified with the full subcategory of
\mathcal{D}(\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}))
of cofibrant quasi-representable dg modules via the Yoneda functor.
Denote by
\mathbb{E}^{\prime}
the corresponding bifunctor of the extriangulated structure on
\mathrm{rep}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
.

Denote by
F
(resp.
G
) the dg functor
k\rightarrow\mathcal{B}=k(0\rightarrow 1)
, sending the object
*
to
0
(resp.
1
).
Let
M
be the
\mathcal{B}
-
k
-bimodule
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{B}}(F(-),-)
and
N
the
k
-
\mathcal{B}
-bimodule
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{B}}(-,G(-))
.
Then we have a morphism of
k
-
k
-bimodules
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{B}}(F(-),G(-))\rightarrow\mathrm{Hom}_{k}(-,-)
which gives rise to a natural isomorphism
{}_{\mathcal{B}}M\otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_{k}-\rightarrow\mathrm{RHom}_{k}(_{k}N_{\mathcal{B}},-)
.
We denote this (isomorphism class of) functor by
H:\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})\rightarrow\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B}^{op}\otimes\mathcal{A})
which sends
X\in\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})
to
X\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}X
.
It restricts to a functor
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})\rightarrow\mathrm{rep}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
which we still denote by
H
.

Let
X\xrightarrow{f}Y
be an object in
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{B}^{op}\otimes\mathcal{A})
and
Z
,
Z^{\prime}
objects in
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})
.
Then we have

(6.47.1)

\displaystyle\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{B}^{op}\otimes\mathcal{A}}(H(Z),X\rightarrow Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{A}}(Z,X)

and

(6.47.2)

\displaystyle\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{B}^{op}\otimes\mathcal{A}}(X\rightarrow Y,H(Z^{\prime}))\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{A}}(Y,Z^{\prime}).

Hence a morphism
H(Z)\rightarrow H(Z^{\prime})
factors through the object
X\xrightarrow{f}Y
if and only if the corresponding morphism
Z\rightarrow Z^{\prime}
factors through the morphism
X\xrightarrow{\overline{f}}Y
.

The dg functor
F
induces a quasi-fully faithful exact morphism
\mathcal{A}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(k,\mathcal{A})\rightarrow\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
in
\mathrm{Hqe}
.
By taking 0-th cohomology, we obtain the (isomorphism class of) functor
H:H^{0}(\mathcal{A})\rightarrow\mathrm{rep}(\mathcal{B},A)
.

Proposition 6.48
.

Let
\mathcal{B}
be the dg category
k\mathrm{Mor}
.
The functor
H:H^{0}(\mathcal{A})\rightarrow\mathrm{rep}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
induces a fully exact embedding
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})/\mathcal{J}\rightarrow\mathrm{rep}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})/[I\rightarrow P]
.

Proof.

Recall
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
is identified with the full subcategory of
\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A})
consisting of cofibrant quasi-representable dg modules. By the above discussion the functor
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})\rightarrow\mathrm{rep}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
induces a fully faithful functor
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})/\mathcal{J}\rightarrow\mathrm{rep}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})/[I\rightarrow P]
.

Let
X,Z
be two objects in
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})
.

Claim: The functor
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})\rightarrow\mathrm{rep}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
induces a canonical map

\alpha_{Z,X}:\mathbb{E}(Z,X)\rightarrow\mathbb{E}^{\prime}(H(Z),H(X))

which is a bijection.

To see this, first notice that, by
6.47.1
and
6.47.2
, conflations in
\mathrm{rep}(\mathrm{Mor},\mathcal{A})
which are images of conflations in
\mathcal{A}
make
I\rightarrow P
projective-injective.
So they are in the exact substructure and hence the above is a well-defined map.
Since
H
is fully faithful, the map
\alpha_{Z,X}
is an injection by Proposition
5.20
.

which corresponds to

6.47.1
.

is a homotopy equivalence.

\mathrm{rep}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces H(X)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces H(Y)}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces(Y\rightarrow Y^{\prime})}

So
\delta^{\prime}=H(c)^{*}H(\delta)=H(c^{*}\delta)
for some automorphism
c:Z\rightarrow Z
.
Thus the map
\alpha_{Z,X}
is a bijection and the functor
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})/\mathcal{J}\rightarrow\mathrm{rep}(\mathrm{Mor},\mathcal{A})/[I\rightarrow P]
is a fully exact embedding.
∎

Combining Proposition-Definition
6.20
, Theorem
6.35
, Theorem
6.43
and Proposition
6.48
, we have

Corollary 6.49
.

H^{0}(\mathcal{A})/\mathcal{J}
is an algebraic extriangulated category.

Let
\mathcal{B}
be a connective dg category.
Let
F:\mathcal{A}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A})
be the universal exact morphism from
\mathcal{A}
to a pretriangulated dg category.
The canonical morphism
F_{*}:\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})\rightarrow\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A}))
induces a canonical morphism in
\mathrm{Hqe}

\varphi:\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}))\rightarrow\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A})).

For objects
X
and
Y
in
\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A})
, the canonical map

\tau_{\leq 0}\mathrm{RHom}(X,Y)\xrightarrow{{}_{\sim}}\tau_{\leq 0}\mathrm{RHom}(F_{*}X,F_{*}Y).

is an isomorphism in
\mathcal{D}(k)
.
Also, by Corollary
3.43
, the canonical map

(6.49.1)

\mathbb{E}(X,Y)\xrightarrow{{}_{\sim}}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{rep}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A}))}(F_{*}X,\Sigma F_{*}Y)

is a bijection.
We do not know whether the same is true for higher extension groups (and hence do not know whether
H^{0}(\varphi)
is a triangle equivalence).
It is interesting to study the morphism
\varphi
as it is closely related to the theory of triangle derivators.

Let
(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{S})
and
(\mathcal{A}^{\prime},\mathcal{S}^{\prime})
be small exact dg categories.
Recall that a morphism
\mathcal{A}\rightarrow\mathcal{A}^{\prime}
in
\mathrm{Hqe}
is exact if the induced functor
\mathcal{H}_{3t}(\mathcal{A})\rightarrow\mathcal{H}_{3t}(\mathcal{A}^{\prime})
sends objects in
\mathcal{S}
to objects in
\mathcal{S}^{\prime}
.
Recall that we denote by
\mathrm{Hqe}_{ex}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A}^{\prime})
the subset of
\mathrm{Hqe}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A}^{\prime})
consisiting of exact morphisms.
Let
\mathcal{C}
be an exact dg category.
A morphism
\mu:\mathcal{A}\otimes\mathcal{A}^{\prime}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}
in
\mathrm{Hqe}
is
biexact
, if for each object
A\in\mathcal{A}
and
A^{\prime}\in\mathcal{A}^{\prime}
, the induced morphisms

\mu_{A,-}:\mathcal{A}^{\prime}\rightarrow\mathcal{C},\;\;\mu_{-,A^{\prime}}:\mathcal{A}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}

are both exact morphisms.
Suppose
\mathcal{A}
and
\mathcal{A}^{\prime}
are connective.
We have universal fully exact embeddings
\mathcal{A}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A})
and
\mathcal{A}^{\prime}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A}^{\prime})
into pretriangulated dg categories.
We denote by
\mathrm{rep}_{dg}^{ex}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A}^{\prime})
the full dg subcategory of
\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A}^{\prime})
consisting of the exact morphisms.

Lemma 6.50
.

Suppose
\mathcal{A}
and
\mathcal{A}^{\prime}
are small connective exact dg categories.
The dg category
\mathrm{rep}_{dg}^{ex}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A}^{\prime})
is stable under extensions in
\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A}^{\prime})
. In particular it inherits a canonical exact dg structure.

Proof.

We have a canonical bijection

\mathrm{Hqe}_{ex}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A}^{\prime})\xrightarrow{{}_{\sim}}\mathrm{Hqe}_{ex}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A}^{\prime}))

and hence by Lemma
3.19
we have a canonical quasi-equivalence

\tau_{\leq 0}\mathrm{rep}_{dg}^{ex}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A}^{\prime})\xrightarrow{{}_{\sim}}\tau_{\leq 0}\mathrm{rep}_{dg}^{ex}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A}^{\prime})).

Since
\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A}^{\prime})
is a pretriangulated dg category,
we have that
\mathrm{rep}^{ex}_{dg}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A}^{\prime}))
is extension-closed in
\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A}^{\prime}))
.
Therefore by the bijection
6.49.1
we have that
\mathrm{rep}_{dg}^{ex}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A}^{\prime})
is an
extension-closed dg subcategory of
\mathrm{rep}_{dg}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A}^{\prime})
.
∎

Let
\mathcal{A}\boxtimes\mathcal{A}^{\prime}
be the
\tau_{\leq 0}
-truncation of the extension closure of the quasi-essential image of the morphism in
\mathrm{Hqe}

F:\mathcal{A}\otimes\mathcal{A}^{\prime}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A})\otimes\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A}^{\prime})\rightarrow\mathrm{pretr}(\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A})\otimes\mathcal{D}^{b}_{dg}(\mathcal{A}^{\prime}))

Proposition 6.51
.

The natural morphism
\mathcal{A}\otimes\mathcal{A}^{\prime}\rightarrow\mathcal{A}\boxtimes\mathcal{A}^{\prime}
is the universal biexact morphism in
\mathrm{Hqe}
from
\mathcal{A}\otimes\mathcal{A}^{\prime}
to an exact dg category.

Proof.

Let
\mathcal{C}
be an exact dg category and
G:\mathcal{A}\otimes\mathcal{A}^{\prime}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}
a biexact morphism in
\mathrm{Hqe}
.
Since
\mathcal{A}\otimes\mathcal{A}^{\prime}
is connective, the morphism
G
factors through
\tau_{\leq 0}\mathcal{C}
.
